question: Can a generative model be trained without Markov chains or approximate inference by pitting it against a discriminator in a minimax game?
hypothesis: Training G to fool D has a unique optimum at p_g = p_data, and with MLPs it can be trained by backpropagation and give competitive samples.
contributions: A minimax adversarial framework for estimating generative models
Proof that the global optimum is p_g = p_data and that Algorithm 1 converges in the non-parametric setting
Experiments on MNIST, TFD and CIFAR-10 with Parzen-window log-likelihood and sample visualisations

method.summary: A generator MLP maps noise z to data space and a discriminator MLP outputs the probability that x is real. They are trained alternately with minibatch SGD with momentum on the minimax value function. Evaluation is Parzen-window log-likelihood of test data plus sample figures.

datasets.name: MNIST
datasets.split: validation set used to cross-validate Parzen sigma; test set for log-likelihood

datasets.name: Toronto Face Database (TFD)
datasets.split: per-fold; sigma chosen on each fold's validation set

models.name: Generator G (MLP)
models.architecture: multilayer perceptron with rectifier and sigmoid activations; noise input only to bottommost layer; a convolutional/'deconvolutional' variant for CIFAR-10

models.name: Discriminator D (MLP)
models.architecture: multilayer perceptron with maxout activations and dropout; scalar output; convolutional variant for CIFAR-10

training.objective: min_G max_D E_x[log D(x)] + E_z[log(1-D(G(z)))]; in practice G maximises log D(G(z)) early in learning
training.dropout: applied in training the discriminator; rate not stated

other.code: hyperparameters said to be at github.com/goodfeli/adversarial

inference.decoding: forward pass of G on z sampled from prior
inference.samples: Parzen window fitted to generated samples; number of samples not stated

metrics.name: Parzen window log-likelihood
metrics.definition: Gaussian Parzen window fitted to samples from G; mean log-likelihood of test data under it; sigma cross-validated on validation set

eval.protocol: MNIST: standard error of the mean across examples; TFD: standard error across folds, sigma cross-validated per fold. MNIST compared against real-valued version of the data.

evidence.quote: We used k = 1, the least expensive option, in our experiments.

results.claim: Adversarial nets reach Parzen log-likelihood 225 on MNIST, above Deep GSN 214, DBN 138 and Stacked CAE 121.
results.setup: MNIST real-valued version, test set mean, SEM across examples, sigma cross-validated
results.table: Table 1, row Adversarial nets, column MNIST

results.claim: On TFD adversarial nets score 2057, below Stacked CAE 2110 and above DBN 1909 and Deep GSN 1890.
results.setup: TFD, SEM across folds, sigma cross-validated per fold on validation set
results.table: Table 1, row Adversarial nets, column TFD

results.claim: At the global optimum the virtual criterion C(G) equals -log 4 and p_g = p_data.
results.setup: Non-parametric limit, optimal D, infinite capacity (theorem, not an experiment)
results.quote: C∗= −log(4) is the global minimum of C(G) and that the only solution is pg = pdata
results.note: Theoretical result; kind labelled measured only as the schema has no proof slot

results.claim: Optimal discriminator for fixed G is p_data/(p_data+p_g), and D = 1/2 at convergence.
Authors say the Parzen estimator has high variance and fails in high dimensions, and make no claim samples beat existing methods.

limits: D must be synchronised with G; training G too much without updating D causes the 'Helvetica scenario' where G collapses many z to the same x.
Parzen window likelihood has 'somewhat high variance and does not perform well in high dimensional spaces'.
Convergence proof holds only in the non-parametric setting; with MLPs there are multiple critical points and no guarantee.
Authors 'make no claim that these samples are better than samples generated by existing methods'.
Architecture sizes, learning rate, batch size, steps and hardware are not given in the paper (code repo referenced).
